one_liner_plain: Two doses of BNT162b2 were 95% effective against Covid-19

citation.title: Safety and Efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 Vaccine
citation.authors: Polack FP, Thomas SJ, Kitchin N, et al.

sections.background: By late 2020, SARS-CoV-2 had infected tens of millions of people, and safe, effective vaccines were needed urgently. BNT162b2 is a lipid nanoparticle-formulated, nucleoside-modified RNA vaccine that encodes a prefusion-stabilized, membrane-anchored version of the full-length SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. C4591001 was its pivotal efficacy trial: could a never-before-licensed vaccine platform prevent Covid-19, and was it safe?

methods.design: Ongoing multinational, placebo-controlled, observer-blinded pivotal efficacy trial (phase 2/3 portion) at 152 sites in the United States, Argentina, Brazil, South Africa, Germany, and Turkey; 1:1 randomization.
methods.population: People 16 years of age or older, including those with stable chronic medical conditions. {{n:n_rand}} underwent randomization; {{n:n_vax}} received BNT162b2 and {{n:n_pbo}} received placebo.
methods.intervention: Two doses of BNT162b2 (30 µg per dose), given intramuscularly 21 days apart.
methods.comparator: Two doses of saline placebo, 21 days apart.
methods.primary_endpoint: Efficacy against laboratory-confirmed Covid-19 with onset at least 7 days after the second dose, and safety (reactogenicity and adverse events).
methods.follow-up: A median of 2 months after the second dose for the main safety data set; the trial was designed to follow participants for 2 years.

sections.results: There were {{n:cases_vax}} cases of Covid-19 with onset at least 7 days after the second dose in the vaccine group and {{n:cases_pbo}} in the placebo group. That works out to {{n:ve}} vaccine efficacy (95% credible interval 90.3 to 97.6), and similar efficacy (generally 90 to 100%) held across subgroups by age, sex, race, ethnicity, body-mass index, and coexisting conditions. Protection started early. Between the first and second doses, efficacy was already {{n:ve_d1}} ({{n:d1_vax}} vs {{n:d1_pbo}} cases). Of the 10 cases of severe Covid-19 after the first dose, {{n:sev_pbo}} were in placebo recipients and {{n:sev_vax}} in a vaccine recipient. Reactogenicity was mostly short-lived and mild to moderate. Injection-site pain was the most common local reaction: {{n:pain_y1}} of younger participants after dose 1 and {{n:pain_o1}} of those older than 55. Fatigue and headache were the most common systemic events, more frequent after dose 2 (younger recipients: {{n:fat_y}} and {{n:head_y}}), though many placebo recipients reported them too ({{n:fat_yp}} and {{n:head_yp}}). Serious adverse events were similar: {{n:sae_vax}} versus {{n:sae_pbo}}.
sections.conclusions: A two-dose regimen of BNT162b2 conferred 95% protection against Covid-19 in people 16 years of age or older, and safety over a median of 2 months was similar to that of other viral vaccines.
sections.limitations: With about 19,000 participants per group in the main safety subset, the trial could not reliably detect less common adverse events. Follow-up was a median of 2 months after dose 2, so longer-term safety and the duration of protection were unknown. The report does not address whether vaccination prevents asymptomatic infection, and the high efficacy left too few breakthrough cases to establish a correlate of protection. Keeping a placebo group for the planned 2 years became ethically and practically impossible once the vaccine was authorized.
sections.practice_impact: C4591001 was the first phase 3 efficacy result for an mRNA vaccine, and it led straight to emergency authorization and mass vaccination in late 2020. It proved the mRNA platform at scale and set the template for rapid, large, event-driven vaccine trials.
